181	Order placement also authorizes payment. `payment_status` starts at `UNPAID` and immediately moves to `AUTHORIZED` as a placement-time side effect; any available `credit_balance_cents` on the customer is drawn down before the card authorization covers the remaining amount. `final_delivery_fee_cents`, `final_commission_cents`, `actual_delivery_time`, and `minutes_late` all start as null and are populated only when the order reaches `DELIVERED`. `version` starts at 1, as for every other versioned resource.
182	
183	### 3.5. Restaurant-Side Order Flow
184	
185	A restaurant that owns the target order can accept it, transitioning the order from `PLACED` to `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`. Acceptance is only legal while the restaurant's own `status` is `ACTIVE` and the order is still in `PLACED`; the restaurant identity is enforced by the `X-User-ID` match against `Order.restaurant_id`. Acceptance does not touch `payment_status` — the order is already `AUTHORIZED` from placement. From `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, the restaurant signals start-preparing, advancing the order to `PREPARING`; this same action opens a dispatch offer to the best available rider, which may — depending on the current rider's route — merge into an existing `RouteGroup`. From `PREPARING`, the restaurant marks the order ready, advancing it to `READY_FOR_PICKUP`. Ready is only legal when a rider has already `ACCEPTED` the dispatch (or is further along at `PICKED_UP`) — the system refuses the ready transition otherwise with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.
186	
187	Either the customer or the restaurant (via rejection) may cancel an order while it is still in `PLACED`; the cancellation transitions the order to `CANCELLED` and moves `payment_status` from whichever of `UNPAID` or `AUTHORIZED` it is currently in to `VOIDED`. No charge has captured, so `credit_balance_cents` is not affected. `CustomerService` may also cancel on behalf of a customer. Cancellation once the order has moved beyond `PLACED` is not available through this channel; disputes at later stages flow through the refund workflow in §3.9.
188	
189	The full set of `Order.status` values is `PLACED`, `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, and `REFUNDED`; the terminal states are `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REFUNDED`. The full set of `payment_status` values is `UNPAID`, `AUTHORIZED`, `CAPTURED`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`, `FULLY_REFUNDED`, and `VOIDED`.
190	
191	### 3.6. Dispatch, Assignment, and Route Merging
192	
193	When a restaurant starts preparing an order, the system opens a dispatch offer — an `Assignment` row linking an `order_id` to a candidate `rider_id`. An assignment begins in `OFFERED` at its `offered_at` timestamp and evolves through `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, and `DELIVERED` in the success path, or `REJECTED` / `CANCELLED` on abandonment. The full set of `Assignment.status` values is `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, `PICKED_UP`, `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED`; `DELIVERED`, `REJECTED`, and `CANCELLED` are terminal.
194	
195	The candidate `rider_id` is selected deterministically from the pool of riders whose `status` is `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY`. Any rider currently linked to an `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP` `Assignment` for the same `order_id` is excluded from this pool up front — the system never re-offers an order to a rider who already holds it, regardless of whether the offer originated from `/start-preparing`, from an explicit `/dispatch`, or from the fresh offer the system issues after a rejection or cancellation. From the surviving candidates the system prefers any rider in `ON_DELIVERY` whose existing `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` already contains at least one unpicked assignment whose pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of the new order's pickup restaurant — these are precisely the riders for whom acceptance would trigger the route-merge rule described two paragraphs below — over any rider in `AVAILABLE`. Within either preference tier the tie-breaker is `Rider.created_at` descending, so that the most recently registered rider wins; should that still tie, the rider whose `id` sorts lexicographically smallest is chosen. The presence of other live `Assignment` rows for the same `order_id` — including one already in `ACCEPTED` or `PICKED_UP` — is not by itself grounds for refusal; `/dispatch` always creates a new `OFFERED` `Assignment` so long as the pool is non-empty, and the uniqueness constraint stated in the next paragraph fires later at `/accept` time rather than at dispatch time. The dispatch is refused with `409 ERR_INVALID_STATE` only when the resulting candidate pool is empty, in which case no new `Assignment` is created.
196	
197	Acceptance by a rider requires that the rider's current `status` be `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY` (the latter is what enables route merging), that the corresponding `Order.status` be `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, or `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, and — critically — that no other `Assignment` already exists for the same `order_id` in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`. When two riders race to accept the same dispatched offer, first-writer-wins on this uniqueness constraint: exactly one assignment advances to `ACCEPTED`, and the losing attempt is rejected with `ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. Acceptance stamps `accepted_at`, cascades the rider's `status` to `ON_DELIVERY` if they were `AVAILABLE`, and triggers a recomputation of `acceptance_rate` over the rider's last 30 offers.
198	
199	Route merging happens at the same moment. When the accepting rider already holds an `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` and the newly accepted order's pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of an existing unpicked assignment's pickup restaurant, the new assignment is attached to that `RouteGroup` — its `route_group_id` is set to the group's `id` and the group's `assignment_ids` array is extended to include the new assignment's `id`. The `RouteGroup` itself tracks its own `rider_id`, `assignment_ids`, `merged_at` timestamp, and `status`, which spans `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, and `ABANDONED`, starting in `ACTIVE`. Solo deliveries leave `route_group_id` null.
200	
201	Rejection of an offer — either explicitly by the rider, or via the 60-second offer-timeout sweep that runs as part of the clock-advance capability — moves the assignment to `REJECTED`, recomputes the rider's `acceptance_rate`, and spawns a fresh `Assignment` for the order targeting the next best available rider.
202	
203	Pickup advances the assignment from `ACCEPTED` to `PICKED_UP`, stamps `picked_up_at`, and cascades the order from `READY_FOR_PICKUP` to `PICKED_UP`. A rider may also cancel an assignment after accepting it but before pickup; this transition is legal only while the assignment is in `ACCEPTED` and the order has not yet reached `PICKED_UP`. Cancellation creates a `Fine` whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `RIDER_NO_SHOW`, with `amount_cents` fixed at 500 — the flat no-show penalty. That fine in turn debits the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by 500 cents and triggers a `bonus_tier` recomputation (this is the transitive chain: the assignment cancellation triggers the fine, and the fine's creation triggers the wallet debit and tier recompute). The system then dispatches a fresh offer for the same order to the next best rider.
204	
205	### 3.7. Delivery and Fiscal Reconciliation
206	
207	The final operational step is delivery. A rider whose assignment is in `PICKED_UP` and whose corresponding order is in `PICKED_UP` invokes the deliver capability. The assignment transitions to `DELIVERED`, `delivered_at` is stamped, and the order cascades to `DELIVERED` as well. A substantial chain of fiscal side-effects fires atomically on this cascade.
208	
209	First, the order's `actual_delivery_time` is set to the current instant, and `minutes_late` is computed as the non-negative floor of the seconds between `actual_delivery_time` and `promised_delivery_time`, divided by 60. Early or on-time deliveries produce a `minutes_late` of zero.
210	
211	Second, the order's `final_delivery_fee_cents` is reconciled from the frozen placement inputs. The solo-style fee is recomputed from the original `distance_km` and `is_peak` snapshots using the same base-of-300, 120-per-band, 200-peak formula as the provisional fee. Then, if the assignment carries a non-null `route_group_id` and its route group contains two or more assignments, a 25% route-merge discount is applied: the discount is computed as the floor of the solo fee times 0.25, and the rider-facing delivery fee is the solo fee minus that discount. Solo deliveries (no `route_group_id`, or a `RouteGroup` containing only this assignment) carry no discount and the final fee equals the solo fee. The reconciled amount is written to both `Order.final_delivery_fee_cents` and `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` — these two mirror each other for any single-leg delivery, and for merged deliveries the platform absorbs the discount as a cost of bundling.
212	
213	Third, the order's `final_commission_cents` is reconciled — and this is where it may diverge from `provisional_commission_cents`. If, at the moment of delivery, the owning restaurant's `commission_rate_override` is a non-null decimal, commission is computed as a flat rate: the subtotal multiplied by that override rate, rounded half-up to a whole cent. The override applies to the entire subtotal, not just the portion above any tier threshold. If `commission_rate_override` is null at delivery time, the same tiered formula described in §3.4 runs again — 15% / 18% / 22% across the same 20 000-cent and 50 000-cent caps, summed in decimal and then rounded half-up once. Because the override can be changed mid-flight by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`, the final commission can legitimately differ from the provisional one even though the subtotal is immutable.
214	
215	Fourth, `payment_status` moves unconditionally to `CAPTURED`.
216	
217	Fifth, if `minutes_late` is greater than zero, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `LATE_DELIVERY`. The fine amount is tiered: when `minutes_late` is from 1 through 10 inclusive, `amount_cents` is a flat 200 cents (a two-dollar penalty); when `minutes_late` is from 11 through 30 inclusive, `amount_cents` is 500 plus 50 per minute over 10 — so a 20-minute lateness yields 500 plus 50 times 10, which is 1 000 cents; when `minutes_late` exceeds 30, `amount_cents` is the smaller of `final_delivery_fee_cents` and 1 500 (the rider's earnings clawback is capped at $15 regardless of the fee) plus an additional 500 cents of customer compensation. This fine creation itself triggers a follow-on debit of the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by `amount_cents` and a recomputation of the rider's `bonus_tier` — the same transitive fan-out chain as the no-show case.
218	
219	Sixth, the owning restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is incremented by `subtotal_cents` minus `final_commission_cents` — the restaurant's slice of the order.
220	
221	Seventh, the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited with the reconciled `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` (net of any merge discount absorbed by the platform) and the rider's `bonus_tier` is recomputed a final time for the delivery event.
222	
223	Eighth, if the assignment belonged to a `RouteGroup` and every peer assignment in that group has also reached `DELIVERED`, the `RouteGroup` transitions from `ACTIVE` to `COMPLETED`. Otherwise the group stays `ACTIVE` and the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`. A rider only returns to `AVAILABLE` once no active assignments remain for them.
224	
225	All of these effects happen as part of the same request. A single rider delivery therefore mutates the assignment, the order, the restaurant, the rider, the fine (when created), and potentially the route group — and each versioned resource in that chain has its `updated_at` refreshed and its `version` incremented exactly once.
226	
227	### 3.8. Restaurant Settlement
228	
229	At each payout cycle, the platform settles with each `ACTIVE` restaurant. A `PlatformAdmin` invokes the restaurant's settle capability; the restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is reset to 0, and the settlement event is treated as the paid-out audit marker. Returns that were approved after a delivery but before the settlement cycle decrement `pending_settlement_cents` at the moment of approval (see §3.9); deliveries increment it. Because both updates are performed atomically as part of the triggering request, the running aggregate is always consistent with the set of `Order` rows in `DELIVERED` that have not been `FULLY_REFUNDED`. The aggregate is never recomputed from scratch; each event applies an incremental delta.
230	
231	### 3.9. Returns and Refunds
232	
233	A customer may open a return on a delivered order. The customer-facing payload carries the return's `reason` — one of `QUALITY_ISSUE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `LATE`, or `OTHER` — and a `requested_refund_cents` amount. The request is only eligible when the order is in `DELIVERED` and the current moment is within 24 hours of the order's `actual_delivery_time`; requests outside that window are rejected with `ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED`. The requested refund must be at least 1 and at most the order's `subtotal_cents`; values out of range are rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. A duplicate return attempt — a request made while another `Return` for the same order is already in `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, or `ESCALATED` — is rejected with `ERR_DUPLICATE_RETURN`.
234	
235	A successful return request creates a `Return` row in `REQUESTED` carrying the `order_id`, the `reason`, the `requested_refund_cents`, and — at decision time — the `reviewer_cs_user_id` that recorded the outcome. The owning `Order` transitions from `DELIVERED` to `REFUND_REQUESTED`. The full set of `Return.status` values is `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, and `ESCALATED`; `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` are terminal.
236	
237	A `CustomerService` operator then reviews. Approval carries an `approved_refund_cents` amount that must be at least 1, at most the order's `subtotal_cents`, and at most the originally requested refund — any violation is rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. On approval, the `Return` moves to `APPROVED` and the owning order cascades from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `REFUNDED`. The order's `payment_status` becomes `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` if `approved_refund_cents` is strictly less than `subtotal_cents`, or `FULLY_REFUNDED` if the approved amount equals the subtotal. The customer's `credit_balance_cents` is credited by `approved_refund_cents`. The restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is decremented by the same amount. And finally, if the customer's `trust_score` is strictly below 0.5 and the return's `reason` is `QUALITY_ISSUE`, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the customer and whose `reason` is `ABUSIVE_RETURN` with `amount_cents` equal to `approved_refund_cents`. The four possible `Fine.reason` values are `LATE_DELIVERY`, `ABUSIVE_RETURN`, `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT`, and `RIDER_NO_SHOW`; a fine's `subject_type` is one of `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER` and its `subject_id` is the matching entity's `id`. A fine's `settlement_status` begins at `PENDING` and can move to `SETTLED` (when the underlying wallet or settlement event has cleared the balance) or `WAIVED` (when a `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` forgives the debit and reverses any wallet or credit adjustment).
238	
239	Rejection by a `CustomerService` operator moves the `Return` to `REJECTED` and reverts the order from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `DELIVERED` with no monetary change. Escalation moves the `Return` from `REQUESTED` to `ESCALATED` and opens a `WorkOrder` linked via `related_return_id` for supervisor attention. An escalated return can be brought back to `REQUESTED` through a reopen step — this closes the linked `WorkOrder`. The approve / reject transitions accept both `REQUESTED` and `ESCALATED` as legal starting states; the reopen transition is only legal from `ESCALATED`.

From the surviving candidates the system prefers any rider in `ON_DELIVERY` whose existing `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` already contains at least one unpicked assignment whose pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of the new order's pickup restaurant — these are precisely the riders for whom acceptance would trigger the route-merge rule described two paragraphs below — over any rider in `AVAILABLE`. Within either preference tier the tie-breaker is `Rider.created_at` descending, so that the most recently registered rider wins; should that still tie, the rider whose `id` sorts lexicographically smallest is chosen. The presence of other live `Assignment` rows for the same `order_id` — including one already in `ACCEPTED` or `PICKED_UP` — is not by itself grounds for refusal; `/dispatch` always creates a new `OFFERED` `Assignment` so long as the pool is non-empty, and the uniqueness constraint stated in the next paragraph fires later at `/accept` time rather than at dispatch time. The dispatch is refused with `409 ERR_INVALID_STATE` only when the resulting candidate pool is empty, in which case no new `Assignment` is created.

Acceptance by a rider requires that the rider's current `status` be `AVAILABLE` or `ON_DELIVERY` (the latter is what enables route merging), that the corresponding `Order.status` be `RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED`, `PREPARING`, or `READY_FOR_PICKUP`, and — critically — that no other `Assignment` already exists for the same `order_id` in `OFFERED`, `ACCEPTED`, or `PICKED_UP`. When two riders race to accept the same dispatched offer, first-writer-wins on this uniqueness constraint: exactly one assignment advances to `ACCEPTED`, and the losing attempt is rejected with `ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. Acceptance stamps `accepted_at`, cascades the rider's `status` to `ON_DELIVERY` if they were `AVAILABLE`, and triggers a recomputation of `acceptance_rate` over the rider's last 30 offers.

Route merging happens at the same moment. When the accepting rider already holds an `ACTIVE` `RouteGroup` and the newly accepted order's pickup restaurant is within 500 metres of an existing unpicked assignment's pickup restaurant, the new assignment is attached to that `RouteGroup` — its `route_group_id` is set to the group's `id` and the group's `assignment_ids` array is extended to include the new assignment's `id`. The `RouteGroup` itself tracks its own `rider_id`, `assignment_ids`, `merged_at` timestamp, and `status`, which spans `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, and `ABANDONED`, starting in `ACTIVE`. Solo deliveries leave `route_group_id` null.

Rejection of an offer — either explicitly by the rider, or via the 60-second offer-timeout sweep that runs as part of the clock-advance capability — moves the assignment to `REJECTED`, recomputes the rider's `acceptance_rate`, and spawns a fresh `Assignment` for the order targeting the next best available rider.

Pickup advances the assignment from `ACCEPTED` to `PICKED_UP`, stamps `picked_up_at`, and cascades the order from `READY_FOR_PICKUP` to `PICKED_UP`. A rider may also cancel an assignment after accepting it but before pickup; this transition is legal only while the assignment is in `ACCEPTED` and the order has not yet reached `PICKED_UP`. Cancellation creates a `Fine` whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `RIDER_NO_SHOW`, with `amount_cents` fixed at 500 — the flat no-show penalty. That fine in turn debits the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by 500 cents and triggers a `bonus_tier` recomputation (this is the transitive chain: the assignment cancellation triggers the fine, and the fine's creation triggers the wallet debit and tier recompute). The system then dispatches a fresh offer for the same order to the next best rider.

### 3.7. Delivery and Fiscal Reconciliation

The final operational step is delivery. A rider whose assignment is in `PICKED_UP` and whose corresponding order is in `PICKED_UP` invokes the deliver capability. The assignment transitions to `DELIVERED`, `delivered_at` is stamped, and the order cascades to `DELIVERED` as well. A substantial chain of fiscal side-effects fires atomically on this cascade.

First, the order's `actual_delivery_time` is set to the current instant, and `minutes_late` is computed as the non-negative floor of the seconds between `actual_delivery_time` and `promised_delivery_time`, divided by 60. Early or on-time deliveries produce a `minutes_late` of zero.

Second, the order's `final_delivery_fee_cents` is reconciled from the frozen placement inputs. The solo-style fee is recomputed from the original `distance_km` and `is_peak` snapshots using the same base-of-300, 120-per-band, 200-peak formula as the provisional fee. Then, if the assignment carries a non-null `route_group_id` and its route group contains two or more assignments, a 25% route-merge discount is applied: the discount is computed as the floor of the solo fee times 0.25, and the rider-facing delivery fee is the solo fee minus that discount. Solo deliveries (no `route_group_id`, or a `RouteGroup` containing only this assignment) carry no discount and the final fee equals the solo fee. The reconciled amount is written to both `Order.final_delivery_fee_cents` and `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` — these two mirror each other for any single-leg delivery, and for merged deliveries the platform absorbs the discount as a cost of bundling.

Third, the order's `final_commission_cents` is reconciled — and this is where it may diverge from `provisional_commission_cents`. If, at the moment of delivery, the owning restaurant's `commission_rate_override` is a non-null decimal, commission is computed as a flat rate: the subtotal multiplied by that override rate, rounded half-up to a whole cent. The override applies to the entire subtotal, not just the portion above any tier threshold. If `commission_rate_override` is null at delivery time, the same tiered formula described in §3.4 runs again — 15% / 18% / 22% across the same 20 000-cent and 50 000-cent caps, summed in decimal and then rounded half-up once. Because the override can be changed mid-flight by the restaurant or a `PlatformAdmin`, the final commission can legitimately differ from the provisional one even though the subtotal is immutable.

Fourth, `payment_status` moves unconditionally to `CAPTURED`.

Fifth, if `minutes_late` is greater than zero, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the rider and whose `reason` is `LATE_DELIVERY`. The fine amount is tiered: when `minutes_late` is from 1 through 10 inclusive, `amount_cents` is a flat 200 cents (a two-dollar penalty); when `minutes_late` is from 11 through 30 inclusive, `amount_cents` is 500 plus 50 per minute over 10 — so a 20-minute lateness yields 500 plus 50 times 10, which is 1 000 cents; when `minutes_late` exceeds 30, `amount_cents` is the smaller of `final_delivery_fee_cents` and 1 500 (the rider's earnings clawback is capped at $15 regardless of the fee) plus an additional 500 cents of customer compensation. This fine creation itself triggers a follow-on debit of the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` by `amount_cents` and a recomputation of the rider's `bonus_tier` — the same transitive fan-out chain as the no-show case.

Sixth, the owning restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is incremented by `subtotal_cents` minus `final_commission_cents` — the restaurant's slice of the order.

Seventh, the rider's `wallet_balance_cents` is credited with the reconciled `Assignment.final_delivery_fee_cents` (net of any merge discount absorbed by the platform) and the rider's `bonus_tier` is recomputed a final time for the delivery event.

Eighth, if the assignment belonged to a `RouteGroup` and every peer assignment in that group has also reached `DELIVERED`, the `RouteGroup` transitions from `ACTIVE` to `COMPLETED`. Otherwise the group stays `ACTIVE` and the rider stays `ON_DELIVERY`. A rider only returns to `AVAILABLE` once no active assignments remain for them.

All of these effects happen as part of the same request. A single rider delivery therefore mutates the assignment, the order, the restaurant, the rider, the fine (when created), and potentially the route group — and each versioned resource in that chain has its `updated_at` refreshed and its `version` incremented exactly once.

### 3.8. Restaurant Settlement

At each payout cycle, the platform settles with each `ACTIVE` restaurant. A `PlatformAdmin` invokes the restaurant's settle capability; the restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is reset to 0, and the settlement event is treated as the paid-out audit marker. Returns that were approved after a delivery but before the settlement cycle decrement `pending_settlement_cents` at the moment of approval (see §3.9); deliveries increment it. Because both updates are performed atomically as part of the triggering request, the running aggregate is always consistent with the set of `Order` rows in `DELIVERED` that have not been `FULLY_REFUNDED`. The aggregate is never recomputed from scratch; each event applies an incremental delta.

### 3.9. Returns and Refunds

A customer may open a return on a delivered order. The customer-facing payload carries the return's `reason` — one of `QUALITY_ISSUE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `LATE`, or `OTHER` — and a `requested_refund_cents` amount. The request is only eligible when the order is in `DELIVERED` and the current moment is within 24 hours of the order's `actual_delivery_time`; requests outside that window are rejected with `ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED`. The requested refund must be at least 1 and at most the order's `subtotal_cents`; values out of range are rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. A duplicate return attempt — a request made while another `Return` for the same order is already in `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, or `ESCALATED` — is rejected with `ERR_DUPLICATE_RETURN`.

A successful return request creates a `Return` row in `REQUESTED` carrying the `order_id`, the `reason`, the `requested_refund_cents`, and — at decision time — the `reviewer_cs_user_id` that recorded the outcome. The owning `Order` transitions from `DELIVERED` to `REFUND_REQUESTED`. The full set of `Return.status` values is `REQUESTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, and `ESCALATED`; `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` are terminal.

A `CustomerService` operator then reviews. Approval carries an `approved_refund_cents` amount that must be at least 1, at most the order's `subtotal_cents`, and at most the originally requested refund — any violation is rejected with `ERR_REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`. On approval, the `Return` moves to `APPROVED` and the owning order cascades from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `REFUNDED`. The order's `payment_status` becomes `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` if `approved_refund_cents` is strictly less than `subtotal_cents`, or `FULLY_REFUNDED` if the approved amount equals the subtotal. The customer's `credit_balance_cents` is credited by `approved_refund_cents`. The restaurant's `pending_settlement_cents` is decremented by the same amount. And finally, if the customer's `trust_score` is strictly below 0.5 and the return's `reason` is `QUALITY_ISSUE`, a `Fine` is created whose subject is the customer and whose `reason` is `ABUSIVE_RETURN` with `amount_cents` equal to `approved_refund_cents`. The four possible `Fine.reason` values are `LATE_DELIVERY`, `ABUSIVE_RETURN`, `RESTAURANT_STOCKOUT`, and `RIDER_NO_SHOW`; a fine's `subject_type` is one of `RIDER`, `RESTAURANT`, or `CUSTOMER` and its `subject_id` is the matching entity's `id`. A fine's `settlement_status` begins at `PENDING` and can move to `SETTLED` (when the underlying wallet or settlement event has cleared the balance) or `WAIVED` (when a `CustomerService` operator or `PlatformAdmin` forgives the debit and reverses any wallet or credit adjustment).

Rejection by a `CustomerService` operator moves the `Return` to `REJECTED` and reverts the order from `REFUND_REQUESTED` to `DELIVERED` with no monetary change. Escalation moves the `Return` from `REQUESTED` to `ESCALATED` and opens a `WorkOrder` linked via `related_return_id` for supervisor attention. An escalated return can be brought back to `REQUESTED` through a reopen step — this closes the linked `WorkOrder`. The approve / reject transitions accept both `REQUESTED` and `ESCALATED` as legal starting states; the reopen transition is only legal from `ESCALATED`.

### 3.2. Customer Accounts

A customer account is registered by a `PlatformAdmin` or by a `CustomerService` operator acting on the customer's behalf. The registration payload carries the customer's `name`, `phone` (unique across all customers), `address`, and geographic coordinates `lat` and `lng`. Two computed fields hang off the account: `credit_balance_cents`, a non-negative integer that accumulates platform credit from refunds and compensation and is drawn down before any fresh card charge on subsequent orders; and `trust_score`, a behavioral aggregate initialized at 1.0 and bounded to `[0.0, 1.0]`, which drops on abusive returns and climbs back on good-faith interactions.

15	Every request to the API must carry two HTTP headers: `X-User-ID`, which identifies the acting user, and `X-User-Role`, which declares the capacity in which they are acting. The platform recognizes five roles, spelled exactly as follows: `Customer`, `Restaurant`, `Rider`, `CustomerService`, and `PlatformAdmin`. A request missing either header, or carrying an `X-User-Role` outside this set, is rejected with `ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED`. A request whose role is recognized but not permitted for the called endpoint is rejected with `ERR_FORBIDDEN`.
16	
17	Role identity binds `X-User-ID` to backing entities as follows. When `X-User-Role` is `Customer`, `X-User-ID` is the `id` of the acting `Customer`; ownership checks on any resource that references a `Customer` compare the resource's foreign-key field (such as `Order.customer_id` or `WorkOrder.opened_by_id` where the opener was a customer) to `X-User-ID`. When `X-User-Role` is `Restaurant`, `X-User-ID` is the `id` of the acting `Restaurant`, and ownership checks compare the resource's `restaurant_id` (for example, on an `Order` or a `MenuItem`) to `X-User-ID`. When `X-User-Role` is `Rider`, `X-User-ID` is the `id` of the acting `Rider`, and ownership checks compare the resource's `rider_id` (for example, on an `Assignment` or a `RouteGroup`) to `X-User-ID`.
18	
19	When `X-User-Role` is `CustomerService`, `X-User-ID` is an opaque operator identifier not tied to any persisted entity; the server may record it — for example, on a `Return` as `reviewer_cs_user_id` when a CS operator approves or rejects, or on a `WorkOrder` as `assigned_cs_user_id` when a CS operator claims the ticket — but it is never compared against the `id` of any entity. The same rule applies when `X-User-Role` is `PlatformAdmin`: the admin's `X-User-ID` is opaque, may be recorded on downstream artifacts as a historical marker, and is never compared to an entity `id`.
20	
21	Identity mismatch — a caller whose role is correct but whose `X-User-ID` does not match the resource the operation targets (for instance, a `Customer` reading another customer's profile, or a `Rider` calling the go-online capability on someone else's rider record) — is rejected with `ERR_FORBIDDEN`.

27	All successful API responses (those with 2xx status codes) follow this standard envelope format in their JSON body:
28

31	  "meta": {
32	    "api_request_id": "req_RANDOMALPHANUM123456",
33	    "api_request_timestamp": "2025-05-24T10:30:00.123Z",
34	    "limit": 10,

content.description: Get Flask up with the standard envelope and error machinery, an in-memory store, logical clock, and a working route stub for /api/restaurants. Must boot and answer 404 with correct envelope.

content.subject: Auth and RBAC matrix
content.description: Header presence (X-User-ID, X-User-Role), role-set validation, ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED. RBAC matrix per endpoint, identity binding per role, ERR_FORBIDDEN on identity mismatch.

content.subject: Restaurants + MenuItems lifecycle
content.description: Register, list, get, patch, approve, suspend (with cascade to PLACED orders), reinstate, settle. MenuItem create/patch/list. ACTIVE-only visibility for orders.

content.subject: Customers and Riders CRUD + lifecycle
content.description: Register customer (PlatformAdmin or CustomerService). Read own only for customers. Register rider, go-online/go-offline, suspend (criteria check).

content.subject: Orders: placement and restaurant flow
content.description: Place an order (subtotal, distance, peak, promised_delivery_time, provisional fees/commission, payment authorize, credit drawdown). Accept, start-preparing (opens dispatch), ready, cancel.

content.subject: Dispatch, Assignments, Route Merging
content.description: Candidate selection (ON_DELIVERY merge preference, AVAILABLE fallback, tie-breakers), accept (uniqueness), reject (redispatch), pickup, cancel (RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + tier recompute + redispatch).

content.subject: Delivery cascade and fiscal reconciliation
content.description: Compute actual_delivery_time, minutes_late, final_delivery_fee (with merge discount), final_commission (override or tiered), payment CAPTURED, late fine (tiered), settlement increment, wallet credit, bonus tier recompute, route group COMPLETED.

content.subject: Returns and refunds
content.description: Open return (within 24h, amount validation, duplicate-check, ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED). Approve (cascade: order REFUNDED, payment status, credit_balance, settlement decrement, abusive return fine when trust_score < 0.5 + QUALITY_ISSUE). Reject, escalate (opens WorkOrder), reopen (closes WorkOrder).

content.subject: Work orders
content.description: Open, assign, request-info, submit-info (opener identity), resolve (requires assigned + linked return resolved), escalate, close. ERR_RELATED_RETURN_UNRESOLVED.

content.subject: Fines: list/read/waive
content.description: Subject-scoped read for Rider/Restaurant/Customer; full access for CS/Admin. Waive reverses ledger (rider wallet credit, customer credit restore, restaurant settlement restore). Only PENDING fines waivable.

content.subject: Clock advance + offer timeout sweep
content.description: /api/_clock/advance with seconds. After advance, sweep OFFERED assignments older than 60s to REJECTED + redispatch (and acceptance_rate recompute).

content.description: Fix gaps identified in audit: route group lazy creation, SETTLED transition for restaurant fines. Add covering tests.

def settle(rid):
    parse_headers()
    require_role("PlatformAdmin")
    r = _load(rid)
    if r["status"] == "CLOSED":
        raise fail("ERR_INVALID_STATE")
    r["pending_settlement_cents"] = 0
    # Any PENDING restaurant fines clear as part of this settlement cycle: the underlying
    # settlement event has cleared the balance (PRD §3.9 definition of SETTLED).
    for f in store.fines.values():
        if (f["subject_type"] == "RESTAURANT" and f["subject_id"] == r["id"]
                and f["settlement_status"] == "PENDING"):
            f["settlement_status"] = "SETTLED"
    bump(r)
    return success(r)

from .client import Client


def setup_basics(c=None, *, rate_override=None):
    """Bring up admin + customer + restaurant + 1 menu item. Returns (Client, ids dict)."""

    rid = rr["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/approve", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
    _, mi = c.post(f"/api/restaurants/{rid}/menu-items",
                   {"name": "burger", "price_cents": 500},
                   role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")

    _, cust = c.post("/api/customers",
                     {"name": "C", "phone": "555-1", "address": "x", "lat": 10.01, "lng": 10.01},
                     role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
    cid = cust["data"]["id"]
    return c, {"rid": rid, "mid": mid, "cid": cid}

    _, r = c.post("/api/riders", {"name": name, "phone": phone},
                  role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")

    c.post(f"/api/riders/{rid}/go-online", role="Rider", user_id=rid)

        "restaurant_id": ids["rid"],

    }, role="Customer", user_id=ids["cid"])

"""Dispatch, candidate selection, route merging, race conditions, cancellation."""
from .client import Client
from .fixtures import setup_basics, register_rider, place_order


def _full_to_preparing(c, ids):
    """Place + accept + start-preparing. Returns oid."""
    _, body = place_order(c, ids)
    oid = body["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    return oid


def run(suite):
    def start_preparing_creates_offer():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider_id = register_rider(c)
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        # Find the assignment created by start-preparing
        s, lst = c.get(f"/api/orders?status=PREPARING", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert s == 200
        # We need at least one assignment in OFFERED for the order; pull it via list-by-rider.
        s, body = c.get("/api/assignments/" + _find_assignment_id(c, oid),
                        role="Rider", user_id=rider_id)
        a = body["data"]
        assert a["status"] == "OFFERED"
        assert a["order_id"] == oid

    def order_already_assigned():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        # accept once
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept",
                         role="Rider", user_id=_assignment_rider(c, aid))
        assert s == 200
        # The other rider — dispatch again should refuse since there's already an ACCEPTED assignment
        # Try to create a second OFFERED for the same order via dispatch — PRD says /dispatch always
        # creates a new OFFERED. So new offer exists; then second accept must hit
        # ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED.
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/dispatch",
                         role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        # Pool may be empty (other rider may not pass merge constraint). Should still produce assignment if pool non-empty.
        if s == 201:
            new_aid = body["data"]["id"]
            new_rider = body["data"]["rider_id"]
            s2, body2 = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{new_aid}/accept",
                                role="Rider", user_id=new_rider)
            assert s2 == 409 and body2["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED"

    def reject_redispatches():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        rider_a = _assignment_rider(c, aid)
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/reject",
                         role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["status"] == "REJECTED"
        # A new OFFERED assignment should exist for the order targeting the other rider
        new_aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        assert new_aid != aid

    def cancel_after_accept_creates_fine_and_redispatches():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")  # so redispatch has a candidate
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        rider_a = _assignment_rider(c, aid)
        # Accept then cancel
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["status"] == "CANCELLED"
        # Rider's wallet should be -500c (RIDER_NO_SHOW)
        s, r_body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider_a}", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert r_body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == -500
        # There should now be a fresh OFFERED to the other rider
        new_aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        assert new_aid != aid

    def dispatch_with_empty_pool_invalid_state():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        # No riders registered -> /start-preparing should still succeed because dispatch failure
        # at start-preparing is swallowed. But /dispatch should ERR_INVALID_STATE.
        _, body = place_order(c, ids)
        oid = body["data"]["id"]
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        s, e = c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/dispatch",
                      role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert s == 409 and e["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE"

    suite.case("start-preparing creates OFFERED assignment", start_preparing_creates_offer)
    suite.case("second accept on same order -> ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED", order_already_assigned)
    suite.case("rider reject -> REJECTED + redispatch", reject_redispatches)
    suite.case("rider cancel after accept -> RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + redispatch",
               cancel_after_accept_creates_fine_and_redispatches)
    suite.case("/dispatch with empty pool -> ERR_INVALID_STATE", dispatch_with_empty_pool_invalid_state)


def _find_assignment_id(c, oid):
    """Find an OFFERED/ACCEPTED/PICKED_UP assignment for the order."""
    from app.server import store
    for a in store.assignments.values():
        if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] in ("OFFERED", "ACCEPTED", "PICKED_UP"):
            return a["id"]
    raise AssertionError(f"no live assignment for order {oid}")


def _assignment_rider(c, aid):
    from app.server import store
    return store.assignments[aid]["rider_id"]

        # Rider wallet credited
        s, r2 = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert r2["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == o["final_delivery_fee_cents"]
        # Rider returned to AVAILABLE (no other assignments)
        assert r2["data"]["status"] == "AVAILABLE"

    def commission_uses_override_at_delivery():
        c, ids = setup_basics(rate_override=0.10)
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        # subtotal 500c -> override 0.10 -> 50c
        assert o["data"]["final_commission_cents"] == 50

    def late_delivery_creates_fine():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        # Advance clock past promised time by 50 minutes (45-min promise + 5 min lateness)
        c.post("/api/_clock/advance", {"seconds": 50 * 60},
               role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        s, _ = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert s == 200
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert o["data"]["minutes_late"] == 5
        # Fine of 200c
        s, fines = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        late_fines = [f for f in fines["data"] if f["reason"] == "LATE_DELIVERY"]
        assert len(late_fines) == 1
        assert late_fines[0]["amount_cents"] == 200
        # Wallet: +final_fee then -200
        s, r = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert r["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == o["data"]["final_delivery_fee_cents"] - 200

    def very_late_delivery_uses_clawback_cap():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        # Advance > 30 min late: 45 min promise + 31 min late = 76 min
        c.post("/api/_clock/advance", {"seconds": 76 * 60},
               role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        s, fines = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        late_fines = [f for f in fines["data"] if f["reason"] == "LATE_DELIVERY"]
        assert len(late_fines) == 1
        # fee for ~1.5km distance => 300 + 2*120 = 540 (no peak) -> capped at 540, plus 500
        # Since exact fee depends on the configured coordinates, just check the formula structure:
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        fee = o["data"]["final_delivery_fee_cents"]
        expected = min(fee, 1500) + 500
        assert late_fines[0]["amount_cents"] == expected

    def deliver_requires_picked_up_status():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider = register_rider(c)
        _, body = place_order(c, ids)
        oid = body["data"]["id"]
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        from app.server import store
        aid = next(a["id"] for a in store.assignments.values()
                   if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        # Skip pickup -> deliver should ERR_INVALID_STATE
        s, _ = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert s == 409

    suite.case("on-time delivery cascade: settlement + wallet + AVAILABLE", on_time_delivery_cascade)
    suite.case("commission override applied at delivery", commission_uses_override_at_delivery)
    suite.case("late delivery -> LATE_DELIVERY fine + wallet net effect", late_delivery_creates_fine)
    suite.case(">30min late uses min(fee, 1500) + 500 clawback", very_late_delivery_uses_clawback_cap)
    suite.case("deliver requires PICKED_UP", deliver_requires_picked_up_status)

content.subject: Skeleton: server, envelope, errors, store, clock
content.description: Get Flask up with the standard envelope and error machinery, an in-memory store, logical clock, and a working route stub for /api/restaurants. Must boot and answer 404 with correct envelope.

content.subject: Auth and RBAC matrix
content.description: Header presence (X-User-ID, X-User-Role), role-set validation, ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED. RBAC matrix per endpoint, identity binding per role, ERR_FORBIDDEN on identity mismatch.

content.subject: Restaurants + MenuItems lifecycle
content.description: Register, list, get, patch, approve, suspend (with cascade to PLACED orders), reinstate, settle. MenuItem create/patch/list. ACTIVE-only visibility for orders.

content.subject: Customers and Riders CRUD + lifecycle
content.description: Register customer (PlatformAdmin or CustomerService). Read own only for customers. Register rider, go-online/go-offline, suspend (criteria check).

content.subject: Orders: placement and restaurant flow
content.description: Place an order (subtotal, distance, peak, promised_delivery_time, provisional fees/commission, payment authorize, credit drawdown). Accept, start-preparing (opens dispatch), ready, cancel.

content.subject: Dispatch, Assignments, Route Merging
content.description: Candidate selection (ON_DELIVERY merge preference, AVAILABLE fallback, tie-breakers), accept (uniqueness), reject (redispatch), pickup, cancel (RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + tier recompute + redispatch).

content.subject: Delivery cascade and fiscal reconciliation
content.description: Compute actual_delivery_time, minutes_late, final_delivery_fee (with merge discount), final_commission (override or tiered), payment CAPTURED, late fine (tiered), settlement increment, wallet credit, bonus tier recompute, route group COMPLETED.

content.subject: Returns and refunds
content.description: Open return (within 24h, amount validation, duplicate-check, ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED). Approve (cascade: order REFUNDED, payment status, credit_balance, settlement decrement, abusive return fine when trust_score < 0.5 + QUALITY_ISSUE). Reject, escalate (opens WorkOrder), reopen (closes WorkOrder).

content.subject: Work orders
content.description: Open, assign, request-info, submit-info (opener identity), resolve (requires assigned + linked return resolved), escalate, close. ERR_RELATED_RETURN_UNRESOLVED.

content.subject: Fines: list/read/waive
content.description: Subject-scoped read for Rider/Restaurant/Customer; full access for CS/Admin. Waive reverses ledger (rider wallet credit, customer credit restore, restaurant settlement restore). Only PENDING fines waivable.

content.subject: Clock advance + offer timeout sweep
content.description: /api/_clock/advance with seconds. After advance, sweep OFFERED assignments older than 60s to REJECTED + redispatch (and acceptance_rate recompute).

content.subject: Self-tests: PRD-rule coverage
content.description: Fix gaps identified in audit: route group lazy creation, SETTLED transition for restaurant fines. Add covering tests.

def route_group_lazy_creation_on_second_accept():
        """When a rider accepts a second concurrent unpicked assignment whose pickup is within 500m,
        a new ACTIVE RouteGroup is lazily created and both assignments are attached to it."""

        _, r2 = c.post("/api/restaurants",
                       {"name": "R2", "address": "addr2", "lat": 10.0, "lng": 10.0},
                       role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")

                        role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        # One rider only.
        rider = register_rider(c, phone="r-merge")
        # Order 1 from R1
        oid1 = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid1 = _find_assignment_id(c, oid1)
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid1}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        # Order 2 from R2 (same customer, same coords -> merge eligible)
        _, body2 = c.post("/api/orders", {
            "customer_id": ids["cid"], "restaurant_id": rid2,
            "items": [{"menu_item_id": mi2["data"]["id"], "quantity": 1}],

        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid2}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider)

"""Dispatch, candidate selection, route merging, race conditions, cancellation."""
from .client import Client
from .fixtures import setup_basics, register_rider, place_order


def _full_to_preparing(c, ids):
    """Place + accept + start-preparing. Returns oid."""
    _, body = place_order(c, ids)
    oid = body["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    return oid


def run(suite):
    def start_preparing_creates_offer():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider_id = register_rider(c)
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        # Find the assignment created by start-preparing
        s, lst = c.get(f"/api/orders?status=PREPARING", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert s == 200
        # We need at least one assignment in OFFERED for the order; pull it via list-by-rider.
        s, body = c.get("/api/assignments/" + _find_assignment_id(c, oid),
                        role="Rider", user_id=rider_id)
        a = body["data"]
        assert a["status"] == "OFFERED"
        assert a["order_id"] == oid

    def order_already_assigned():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        # accept once
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept",
                         role="Rider", user_id=_assignment_rider(c, aid))
        assert s == 200
        # The other rider — dispatch again should refuse since there's already an ACCEPTED assignment
        # Try to create a second OFFERED for the same order via dispatch — PRD says /dispatch always
        # creates a new OFFERED. So new offer exists; then second accept must hit
        # ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED.
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/dispatch",
                         role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        # Pool may be empty (other rider may not pass merge constraint). Should still produce assignment if pool non-empty.
        if s == 201:
            new_aid = body["data"]["id"]
            new_rider = body["data"]["rider_id"]
            s2, body2 = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{new_aid}/accept",
                                role="Rider", user_id=new_rider)
            assert s2 == 409 and body2["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED"

    def reject_redispatches():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        rider_a = _assignment_rider(c, aid)
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/reject",
                         role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["status"] == "REJECTED"
        # A new OFFERED assignment should exist for the order targeting the other rider
        new_aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        assert new_aid != aid

    def cancel_after_accept_creates_fine_and_redispatches():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider1 = register_rider(c, phone="r1")
        rider2 = register_rider(c, phone="r2")  # so redispatch has a candidate
        oid = _full_to_preparing(c, ids)
        aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        rider_a = _assignment_rider(c, aid)
        # Accept then cancel
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["status"] == "CANCELLED"
        # Rider's wallet should be -500c (RIDER_NO_SHOW)
        s, r_body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider_a}", role="Rider", user_id=rider_a)
        assert r_body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == -500
        # There should now be a fresh OFFERED to the other rider
        new_aid = _find_assignment_id(c, oid)
        assert new_aid != aid

    def dispatch_with_empty_pool_invalid_state():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        # No riders registered -> /start-preparing should still succeed because dispatch failure
        # at start-preparing is swallowed. But /dispatch should ERR_INVALID_STATE.
        _, body = place_order(c, ids)
        oid = body["data"]["id"]
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        s, e = c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/dispatch",
                      role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert s == 409 and e["data"]["error_id"] == "ERR_INVALID_STATE"

    suite.case("start-preparing creates OFFERED assignment", start_preparing_creates_offer)
    suite.case("second accept on same order -> ERR_ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED", order_already_assigned)
    suite.case("rider reject -> REJECTED + redispatch", reject_redispatches)
    suite.case("rider cancel after accept -> RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + redispatch",
               cancel_after_accept_creates_fine_and_redispatches)
    suite.case("/dispatch with empty pool -> ERR_INVALID_STATE", dispatch_with_empty_pool_invalid_state)


def _find_assignment_id(c, oid):
    """Find an OFFERED/ACCEPTED/PICKED_UP assignment for the order."""
    from app.server import store
    for a in store.assignments.values():
        if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] in ("OFFERED", "ACCEPTED", "PICKED_UP"):
            return a["id"]
    raise AssertionError(f"no live assignment for order {oid}")


def _assignment_rider(c, aid):
    from app.server import store
    return store.assignments[aid]["rider_id"]

"""Delivery cascade: late fine, commission reconciliation, settlement, wallet, route group."""
from .client import Client
from .fixtures import setup_basics, register_rider, place_order


def _drive_to_pickup(c, ids):
    rider = register_rider(c)
    _, body = place_order(c, ids)
    oid = body["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    from app.server import store
    aid = next(a["id"] for a in store.assignments.values() if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/ready", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/pickup", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
    return rider, oid, aid


def run(suite):
    def on_time_delivery_cascade():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        # Deliver immediately (well before 45 min) -> minutes_late=0
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert s == 200
        # Order
        s, o_body = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        o = o_body["data"]
        assert o["status"] == "DELIVERED"
        assert o["payment_status"] == "CAPTURED"
        assert o["minutes_late"] == 0
        assert o["actual_delivery_time"] is not None
        # Final fee == solo fee for a single-leg delivery
        assert o["final_delivery_fee_cents"] is not None
        assert o["final_commission_cents"] is not None
        # Restaurant settlement = subtotal - final_commission
        s, r_body = c.get(f"/api/restaurants/{ids['rid']}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert r_body["data"]["pending_settlement_cents"] == o["subtotal_cents"] - o["final_commission_cents"]
        # Rider wallet credited
        s, r2 = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert r2["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == o["final_delivery_fee_cents"]
        # Rider returned to AVAILABLE (no other assignments)
        assert r2["data"]["status"] == "AVAILABLE"

    def commission_uses_override_at_delivery():
        c, ids = setup_basics(rate_override=0.10)
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        # subtotal 500c -> override 0.10 -> 50c
        assert o["data"]["final_commission_cents"] == 50

    def late_delivery_creates_fine():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        # Advance clock past promised time by 50 minutes (45-min promise + 5 min lateness)
        c.post("/api/_clock/advance", {"seconds": 50 * 60},
               role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        s, _ = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert s == 200
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        assert o["data"]["minutes_late"] == 5
        # Fine of 200c
        s, fines = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        late_fines = [f for f in fines["data"] if f["reason"] == "LATE_DELIVERY"]
        assert len(late_fines) == 1
        assert late_fines[0]["amount_cents"] == 200
        # Wallet: +final_fee then -200
        s, r = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert r["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == o["data"]["final_delivery_fee_cents"] - 200

    def very_late_delivery_uses_clawback_cap():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, oid, aid = _drive_to_pickup(c, ids)
        # Advance > 30 min late: 45 min promise + 31 min late = 76 min
        c.post("/api/_clock/advance", {"seconds": 76 * 60},
               role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        s, fines = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        late_fines = [f for f in fines["data"] if f["reason"] == "LATE_DELIVERY"]
        assert len(late_fines) == 1
        # fee for ~1.5km distance => 300 + 2*120 = 540 (no peak) -> capped at 540, plus 500
        # Since exact fee depends on the configured coordinates, just check the formula structure:
        s, o = c.get(f"/api/orders/{oid}", role="PlatformAdmin", user_id="op")
        fee = o["data"]["final_delivery_fee_cents"]
        expected = min(fee, 1500) + 500
        assert late_fines[0]["amount_cents"] == expected

    def deliver_requires_picked_up_status():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider = register_rider(c)
        _, body = place_order(c, ids)
        oid = body["data"]["id"]
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
        from app.server import store
        aid = next(a["id"] for a in store.assignments.values()
                   if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
        c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        # Skip pickup -> deliver should ERR_INVALID_STATE
        s, _ = c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/deliver", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert s == 409

    suite.case("on-time delivery cascade: settlement + wallet + AVAILABLE", on_time_delivery_cascade)
    suite.case("commission override applied at delivery", commission_uses_override_at_delivery)
    suite.case("late delivery -> LATE_DELIVERY fine + wallet net effect", late_delivery_creates_fine)
    suite.case(">30min late uses min(fee, 1500) + 500 clawback", very_late_delivery_uses_clawback_cap)

"""Fines: scoped list/read, waive reverses ledger."""
from .client import Client
from .fixtures import setup_basics, register_rider, place_order


def _create_no_show_fine(c, ids):
    """Drive an assignment to ACCEPTED then cancel to mint a RIDER_NO_SHOW fine. Returns (rider_id, fine_id)."""
    rider = register_rider(c, phone="r-fines-a")
    # Need a 2nd rider so cancellation's redispatch can still find a candidate (not required)
    register_rider(c, phone="r-fines-b")
    _, body = place_order(c, ids)
    oid = body["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    from app.server import store
    aid = next(a["id"] for a in store.assignments.values()
               if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    accepting_rider = store.assignments[aid]["rider_id"]
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=accepting_rider)
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=accepting_rider)
    fid = next(f["id"] for f in store.fines.values()
               if f["reason"] == "RIDER_NO_SHOW" and f["subject_id"] == accepting_rider)
    return accepting_rider, fid


def run(suite):
    def list_scoped_to_own_for_rider():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        r1, _ = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        # Another fine for a different rider
        c2, ids2 = setup_basics()
        r2, _ = _create_no_show_fine(c2, ids2)
        # r1 must not see r2's fines
        s, body = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=r1)
        assert s == 200
        for f in body["data"]:
            assert f["subject_id"] == r1

    def waive_reverses_wallet_debit():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        s, body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        wallet_before = body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"]
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/fines/{fid}/waive",
                         role="CustomerService", user_id="cs-1")
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["settlement_status"] == "WAIVED"
        s, body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == wallet_before + 500

    def cannot_waive_settled():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        from app.server import store
        store.fines[fid]["settlement_status"] = "SETTLED"
        s, e = c.post(f"/api/fines/{fid}/waive",
                      role="CustomerService", user_id="cs-1")
        assert s == 409

    def rider_cannot_query_other_rider():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        # Try to query with a different rider as the X-User-ID + explicit subject_id pointing at our rider
        s, e = c.get(f"/api/fines?subject_id={rider}",

"""Fines: scoped list/read, waive reverses ledger."""
from .client import Client
from .fixtures import setup_basics, register_rider, place_order


def _create_no_show_fine(c, ids):
    """Drive an assignment to ACCEPTED then cancel to mint a RIDER_NO_SHOW fine. Returns (rider_id, fine_id)."""
    rider = register_rider(c, phone="r-fines-a")
    # Need a 2nd rider so cancellation's redispatch can still find a candidate (not required)
    register_rider(c, phone="r-fines-b")
    _, body = place_order(c, ids)
    oid = body["data"]["id"]
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/accept", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    c.post(f"/api/orders/{oid}/start-preparing", role="Restaurant", user_id=ids["rid"])
    from app.server import store
    aid = next(a["id"] for a in store.assignments.values()
               if a["order_id"] == oid and a["status"] == "OFFERED")
    accepting_rider = store.assignments[aid]["rider_id"]
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/accept", role="Rider", user_id=accepting_rider)
    c.post(f"/api/assignments/{aid}/cancel", role="Rider", user_id=accepting_rider)
    fid = next(f["id"] for f in store.fines.values()
               if f["reason"] == "RIDER_NO_SHOW" and f["subject_id"] == accepting_rider)
    return accepting_rider, fid


def run(suite):
    def list_scoped_to_own_for_rider():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        r1, _ = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        # Another fine for a different rider
        c2, ids2 = setup_basics()
        r2, _ = _create_no_show_fine(c2, ids2)
        # r1 must not see r2's fines
        s, body = c.get("/api/fines", role="Rider", user_id=r1)
        assert s == 200
        for f in body["data"]:
            assert f["subject_id"] == r1

    def waive_reverses_wallet_debit():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        s, body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        wallet_before = body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"]
        s, body = c.post(f"/api/fines/{fid}/waive",
                         role="CustomerService", user_id="cs-1")
        assert s == 200 and body["data"]["settlement_status"] == "WAIVED"
        s, body = c.get(f"/api/riders/{rider}", role="Rider", user_id=rider)
        assert body["data"]["wallet_balance_cents"] == wallet_before + 500

    def cannot_waive_settled():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        from app.server import store
        store.fines[fid]["settlement_status"] = "SETTLED"
        s, e = c.post(f"/api/fines/{fid}/waive",
                      role="CustomerService", user_id="cs-1")
        assert s == 409

    def rider_cannot_query_other_rider():
        c, ids = setup_basics()
        rider, fid = _create_no_show_fine(c, ids)
        # Try to query with a different rider as the X-User-ID + explicit subject_id pointing at our rider
        s, e = c.get(f"/api/fines?subject_id={rider}",
                     role="Rider", user_id="other-rider")
        assert s == 403

    suite.case("rider sees only own fines on /api/fines", list_scoped_to_own_for_rider)
    suite.case("waive PENDING -> WAIVED + ledger reversed", waive_reverses_wallet_debit)
    suite.case("waive SETTLED -> ERR_INVALID_STATE", cannot_waive_settled)

content.subject: Skeleton: server, envelope, errors, store, clock
content.description: Get Flask up with the standard envelope and error machinery, an in-memory store, logical clock, and a working route stub for /api/restaurants. Must boot and answer 404 with correct envelope.

content.subject: Auth and RBAC matrix
content.description: Header presence (X-User-ID, X-User-Role), role-set validation, ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED. RBAC matrix per endpoint, identity binding per role, ERR_FORBIDDEN on identity mismatch.

content.subject: Restaurants + MenuItems lifecycle
content.description: Register, list, get, patch, approve, suspend (with cascade to PLACED orders), reinstate, settle. MenuItem create/patch/list. ACTIVE-only visibility for orders.

content.subject: Customers and Riders CRUD + lifecycle
content.description: Register customer (PlatformAdmin or CustomerService). Read own only for customers. Register rider, go-online/go-offline, suspend (criteria check).

content.subject: Orders: placement and restaurant flow
content.description: Place an order (subtotal, distance, peak, promised_delivery_time, provisional fees/commission, payment authorize, credit drawdown). Accept, start-preparing (opens dispatch), ready, cancel.

content.subject: Dispatch, Assignments, Route Merging
content.description: Candidate selection (ON_DELIVERY merge preference, AVAILABLE fallback, tie-breakers), accept (uniqueness), reject (redispatch), pickup, cancel (RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + tier recompute + redispatch).

content.subject: Delivery cascade and fiscal reconciliation
content.description: Compute actual_delivery_time, minutes_late, final_delivery_fee (with merge discount), final_commission (override or tiered), payment CAPTURED, late fine (tiered), settlement increment, wallet credit, bonus tier recompute, route group COMPLETED.

content.subject: Returns and refunds
content.description: Open return (within 24h, amount validation, duplicate-check, ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED). Approve (cascade: order REFUNDED, payment status, credit_balance, settlement decrement, abusive return fine when trust_score < 0.5 + QUALITY_ISSUE). Reject, escalate (opens WorkOrder), reopen (closes WorkOrder).

content.subject: Work orders
content.description: Open, assign, request-info, submit-info (opener identity), resolve (requires assigned + linked return resolved), escalate, close. ERR_RELATED_RETURN_UNRESOLVED.

content.subject: Fines: list/read/waive
content.description: Subject-scoped read for Rider/Restaurant/Customer; full access for CS/Admin. Waive reverses ledger (rider wallet credit, customer credit restore, restaurant settlement restore). Only PENDING fines waivable.

content.subject: Clock advance + offer timeout sweep
content.description: /api/_clock/advance with seconds. After advance, sweep OFFERED assignments older than 60s to REJECTED + redispatch (and acceptance_rate recompute).

content.description: Fix gaps identified in audit: route group lazy creation, SETTLED transition for restaurant fines. Add covering tests.

I have enough context to produce the audit. The reminder is a gentle nudge but task tracking for this read-only audit isn't useful — I'll just deliver the report.

# Coverage Gaps in PRD vs `tests/`

Sorted by impact, highest first:

- **Bonus tier recompute cascade (PRD §3.3, §3.6/§3.7) — never asserted end-to-end.** `test_formulas.py` covers `bonus_tier()` math; no test verifies that delivering / fining / cancelling actually mutates `Rider.bonus_tier` (or that `on_time_rate`/`acceptance_rate` rolling-30 windows recompute). The "tier ticks after fine creation" branch is unobserved.
- **Late-fine middle tier (11–30 min) in the integration path (PRD §3.7).** `test_formulas` checks the formula, but the only E2E late case in `test_delivery.py` is 5-min (tier 1) and 31-min (tier 3). The `500 + 50*(minutes_late-10)` branch is not exercised through `/deliver`.
- **Commission override mid-flight divergence (PRD §3.7).** No test changes `commission_rate_override` between placement and delivery to assert `provisional_commission_cents != final_commission_cents`. Also missing: override changing from null→value or value→null after placement.

29	def _load(oid):
30	    o = store.orders.get(oid)
31	    if not o:
32	        raise fail("ERR_NOT_FOUND")
33	    return o
34	
35	
36	def create():
37	    user_id, role = parse_headers()
38	    require_role("Customer")
39	    body = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
40	    customer_id = body.get("customer_id")
41	    restaurant_id = body.get("restaurant_id")
42	    items = body.get("items")
43	    if customer_id is None or restaurant_id is None:
44	        raise fail("ERR_VALIDATION", "customer_id and restaurant_id required")
45	    customer = store.customers.get(customer_id)
46	    if not customer:
47	        raise fail("ERR_NOT_FOUND")
48	    restaurant = store.restaurants.get(restaurant_id)
49	    if not restaurant:
50	        raise fail("ERR_NOT_FOUND")
51	    if user_id != customer_id:
52	        raise fail("ERR_FORBIDDEN")
53	
54	    if not isinstance(items, list) or len(items) == 0:
55	        raise fail("ERR_ORDER_INVALID", "items must be a non-empty list")
56	    # Validate menu items exist before unavailability/shape checks
57	    seen_items = []
58	    for it in items:
59	        if not isinstance(it, dict):
60	            raise fail("ERR_VALIDATION", "each item must be an object")
61	        mi_id = it.get("menu_item_id")
62	        if mi_id is None:
63	            raise fail("ERR_VALIDATION", "menu_item_id required")
64	        if mi_id not in store.menu_items:
65	            raise fail("ERR_NOT_FOUND")
66	        seen_items.append((it, store.menu_items[mi_id]))
67	
68	    if restaurant["status"] != "ACTIVE":
69	        raise fail("ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE", "restaurant is not ACTIVE")
70	    for it, mi in seen_items:
71	        if mi["restaurant_id"] != restaurant_id or not mi["is_listed"]:
72	            raise fail("ERR_RESTAURANT_UNAVAILABLE", "menu item unavailable")
73	
74	    subtotal = 0
75	    snapshot_items = []
76	    for it, mi in seen_items:
77	        qty = it.get("quantity")
78	        if not isinstance(qty, int) or isinstance(qty, bool) or qty < 1:
79	            raise fail("ERR_ORDER_INVALID", "quantity must be int >= 1")
80	        unit = mi["price_cents"]
81	        subtotal += unit * qty
82	        snapshot_items.append({
83	            "menu_item_id": mi["id"],
84	            "name": mi["name"],
85	            "unit_price_cents": unit,
86	            "quantity": qty,
87	        })
88	    if subtotal < 100:
89	        raise fail("ERR_ORDER_INVALID", "subtotal must be >= 100 cents")
90	
91	    now = clock.now()
92	    distance_km = haversine_km(restaurant["lat"], restaurant["lng"], customer["lat"], customer["lng"])
93	    is_peak = is_peak_at(now)
94	    provisional_delivery = delivery_fee_solo(distance_km, is_peak)
95	    if restaurant["commission_rate_override"] is not None:
96	        # Provisional commission still uses the tiered formula per §3.4 — override only matters on delivery.
97	        # PRD §3.4 says provisional uses tiered. §3.7 says override applies at delivery reconciliation.
98	        provisional_commission = commission_tiered(subtotal)
99	    else:
100	        provisional_commission = commission_tiered(subtotal)
101	
102	    promised = now + timedelta(minutes=45)
103	    rec = stamp_new()
104	    rec.update({
105	        "customer_id": customer_id,
106	        "restaurant_id": restaurant_id,
107	        "items": snapshot_items,
108	        "subtotal_cents": subtotal,
109	        "distance_km": distance_km,
110	        "is_peak": is_peak,
111	        "promised_delivery_time": format_iso(promised),
112	        "provisional_delivery_fee_cents": provisional_delivery,
113	        "provisional_commission_cents": provisional_commission,
114	        "final_delivery_fee_cents": None,
115	        "final_commission_cents": None,
116	        "actual_delivery_time": None,
117	        "minutes_late": None,
118	        "status": "PLACED",
119	        "payment_status": "UNPAID",
120	    })
121	
122	    # Payment authorization side-effect: draw down credit, then card-authorize the remainder.
123	    total_due = subtotal + provisional_delivery
124	    credit_used = min(customer["credit_balance_cents"], total_due)
125	    customer["credit_balance_cents"] -= credit_used
126	    bump(customer)
127	    rec["credit_used_cents"] = credit_used
128	    rec["card_authorized_cents"] = total_due - credit_used
129	    rec["payment_status"] = "AUTHORIZED"
130	
131	    store.orders[rec["id"]] = rec
132	    return success(rec, status=201)

content.subject: Skeleton: server, envelope, errors, store, clock
content.description: Get Flask up with the standard envelope and error machinery, an in-memory store, logical clock, and a working route stub for /api/restaurants. Must boot and answer 404 with correct envelope.

content.subject: Auth and RBAC matrix
content.description: Header presence (X-User-ID, X-User-Role), role-set validation, ERR_AUTH_REQUIRED. RBAC matrix per endpoint, identity binding per role, ERR_FORBIDDEN on identity mismatch.

content.subject: Restaurants + MenuItems lifecycle
content.description: Register, list, get, patch, approve, suspend (with cascade to PLACED orders), reinstate, settle. MenuItem create/patch/list. ACTIVE-only visibility for orders.

content.subject: Customers and Riders CRUD + lifecycle
content.description: Register customer (PlatformAdmin or CustomerService). Read own only for customers. Register rider, go-online/go-offline, suspend (criteria check).

content.subject: Orders: placement and restaurant flow
content.description: Place an order (subtotal, distance, peak, promised_delivery_time, provisional fees/commission, payment authorize, credit drawdown). Accept, start-preparing (opens dispatch), ready, cancel.

content.subject: Dispatch, Assignments, Route Merging
content.description: Candidate selection (ON_DELIVERY merge preference, AVAILABLE fallback, tie-breakers), accept (uniqueness), reject (redispatch), pickup, cancel (RIDER_NO_SHOW fine + wallet debit + tier recompute + redispatch).

content.subject: Delivery cascade and fiscal reconciliation
content.description: Compute actual_delivery_time, minutes_late, final_delivery_fee (with merge discount), final_commission (override or tiered), payment CAPTURED, late fine (tiered), settlement increment, wallet credit, bonus tier recompute, route group COMPLETED.

content.subject: Returns and refunds
content.description: Open return (within 24h, amount validation, duplicate-check, ERR_RETURN_WINDOW_EXPIRED). Approve (cascade: order REFUNDED, payment status, credit_balance, settlement decrement, abusive return fine when trust_score < 0.5 + QUALITY_ISSUE). Reject, escalate (opens WorkOrder), reopen (closes WorkOrder).

content.subject: Work orders
content.description: Open, assign, request-info, submit-info (opener identity), resolve (requires assigned + linked return resolved), escalate, close. ERR_RELATED_RETURN_UNRESOLVED.

content.subject: Fines: list/read/waive
content.description: Subject-scoped read for Rider/Restaurant/Customer; full access for CS/Admin. Waive reverses ledger (rider wallet credit, customer credit restore, restaurant settlement restore). Only PENDING fines waivable.

content.subject: Clock advance + offer timeout sweep
content.description: /api/_clock/advance with seconds. After advance, sweep OFFERED assignments older than 60s to REJECTED + redispatch (and acceptance_rate recompute).

content.subject: Self-tests: PRD-rule coverage
content.description: Fix gaps identified in audit: route group lazy creation, SETTLED transition for restaurant fines. Add covering tests.
